definition: To make something bad less severe, serious, or painful.
collocations: mitigate the effects of climate change
exampleSentences: Municipal councils must implement sustainable drainage networks to mitigate flood risks in urban developments.
Effective carbon tax policies can help mitigate the long-term impacts of greenhouse gas emissions.

definition: Present, appearing, or found everywhere; omnipresent.
exampleSentences: Smartphones have evolved from luxury gadgets into ubiquitous tools indispensable for modern commerce.
The ubiquitous nature of automated surveillance cameras has ignited vigorous debates over individual privacy rights.

definition: A noticeable and usually unfair difference or inequality between groups or quantities.
exampleSentences: Subsidized vocational schooling can bridge the widening income disparity between rural and metropolitan populations.
Policymakers must confront regional healthcare disparities to ensure equitable life expectancy.
